summary: Alexander Johnston (1775–1849) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served on the Executive Council of Ceylon (~1811–1819) as chief justice and first member, and was Vice-President of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (~1823–1849).

Alexander Kabanoff (1952–2000) was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. In 2000, he was attested as a Senior Researcher at Saint Petersburg State University and head of the Japanese section at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Alexander Lubotsky (born 1956) is a linguist and scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Moscow State University (~1973–1978) and Leiden University (~1979–1987), where he later held a post in 1999.

Alexander O. Hsu specializes in Buddhist, religious, and Sinological studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~2011–2018), supervised by Paul Copp and Christian K. Wedemeyer, and held a teaching position at North Dakota State University (~2017–2018).

Alexander Piatigorsky (1929–2009) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Moscow University (~1946–1951) and under George Roerich (~1957–1960). His career included posts at the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1956–1974), Moscow State University, and SOAS (attested 1995).

Alexander Rogers (1825–1910) was an Indologist and scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the East India Company College (~1843–1845) and served in the Indian Civil Service (~1845–1879).

Alexander Rödel is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He earned an MSc by Research at the University of Edinburgh under the supervision of Steven Sutcliffe and Jeanne Openshaw (attested 2008).

Alexander W. Macdonald (1923–2018) worked in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He held posts at the Musée de l'Homme (attested 1972) and Paris Nanterre University, where he was a professor (attested 1988–1990).

Alexander Wynne (born 1974) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Bristol (~1995–1998) under Paul Williams and Rupert Gethin, and completed a DPhil at the University of Oxford (2000–2003) supervised by Richard Gombrich.

Alexander Yiannopoulos is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and worked under supervisor Karin Myers (attested 2012–2017) along with several other teachers.

Alexander von Rospatt is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of London and earned his PhD under Lambert Schmithausen at the University of Hamburg. He held posts at Leipzig University (attested 1995) and UC Berkeley (attested 2011–2013).

Alexander von Staël-Holstein (1877–1937) was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and Sinologist. He studied at Dorpat, Berlin, Halle-Wittenberg, and Harvard. He held posts at Peking University (~1921–1937) and served as director of the Sino-Indian Institute (~1927–1937).
Alexandra van der Geer is a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. She studied under Leendert A. van Daalen, Henk Bodewitz, and Paul Yves Sondaar.
Alexandre Langlois (1788–1854) was an Indologist who studied under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He was a member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres from ~1835 to 1854.

Alexis Sanderson (born 1948) is an Indologist. He studied at Balliol College and with Lakshman Joo (1972). He was a fellow at Merton and Brasenose, and spent his career at Oxford (~1977–2015), including as professor and fellow of All Souls (~1992–2015).

Alf Hiltebeitel (1942–2023) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Haverford College (~1959–1963) and the University of Chicago (~1964–1973), and served as Professor of Religion and Religious Studies at George Washington University (~1968–2017).
Alfons Fürst (born 1961) is an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Tübingen (~1982–1991) and held a post at the University of Münster (~2006).

Alfonsa Ferrari (1918–1954) was an Indologist and Tibetologist. She studied at Sapienza University of Rome (~1937–1941) under Giuseppe Tucci and Carlo Formichi, and subsequently conducted post-graduate research there.

Alfred Bloom (1926–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Pennsylvania, Andover Newton, and Harvard (PhD ~1956–1963), he held posts at Harvard, served as Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1986–1994), and was Emeritus Professor at Hawaii.

Alfred Cooper Woolner (1878–1936) was an Indologist and linguist. Educated at Trinity College, Oxford (~1897–1901), he served as Principal of Oriental College, Lahore (~1903–1928), Honorary Librarian at Panjab University (~1903–1928), and Vice-Chancellor of the University of the Punjab (~1928–1936).
